result: In 41 CFS vs 30 controls, AIx@75 was higher (22.5 vs 13.3%, P=0.002), as were CRP (2.58 vs 1.07 ug/ml) and 8-iso-PGF2alpha isoprostanes (470.7 vs 331.1 pg/ml, P<0.005); AIx correlated with logCRP (r=0.51), isoprostanes (r=0.37) and oxidised LDL (r=0.33).
reason: Raised isoprostanes and oxidised LDL are oxidative-stress markers in the same direction; the link to arterial stiffness adds something new.

result: In a 53-year prospective birth cohort (2983 assessed, 34 with CFS, 1.1%), CFS was not preceded by childhood illness or atopy; more exercise in childhood and early adulthood and lower BMI predicted later CFS, and cases kept exercising after early fatigue began.
reason: This supports the claim that deconditioning does not explain the illness, so 'contradicts' is wrong. It uses a different design (premorbid self-reported activity, not exercise physiology).

result: In a population-based Wichita sample (28 CFS, 35 ISF, 39 non-fatigued), CFS had lower morning and higher evening salivary cortisol (a flattened diurnal profile); IL-6 was highest in CFS but not significant after BMI adjustment.
reason: Independent cohort, same measure (salivary morning cortisol), lower in the same direction; not among the cited studies.

result: On 70-degree tilt in 26 adolescents with CFS vs matched controls, 13 CFS vs 5 controls had orthostatic intolerance (sensitivity 50%, specificity 80.8%), and 7 CFS (27%) vs 0 controls had POTS without hypotension.
reason: Adolescent POTS rate of about 27% vs 0 in controls falls in the finding's minority range; independent cohort.

result: Sympathetic predominance in HRV during tilt was described only in tilt-positive CFS subjects, with no control comparison or numbers.
reason: The abstract gives no resting HR or HF-HRV comparison with controls, so it is too thin to test the finding; the paper is already covered by the POTS link.

result: In a Georgia population-based sample (75 medication-free CFS, 110 well controls), the morning salivary cortisol profile (waking, +30, +60 min) was attenuated in CFS; this held in women only, not men.
reason: Same measure (salivary awakening cortisol), same direction, independent population cohort; the sex-specific effect adds detail.

result: Attenuated morning cortisol in CFS was limited to women.
reason: The finding is about sex differences in prevalence and genetic risk; the paper measures cortisol by sex, not prevalence. It is already covered by the low-cortisol link.

result: 15 adolescents with CFS vs 56 controls had higher resting heart rate, diastolic BP and plasma noradrenaline (P<0.01) and adrenaline (P<0.05), a larger HR rise during LBNP and a smaller rise during handgrip.
reason: Replicates the higher resting HR (HRV was not measured); the raised plasma adrenaline also fits the newer neuro-plasma-adrenaline finding.

result: In 34 female CFS patients vs 25 controls, salivary cortisol after 0.5 mg dexamethasone was lower before (p=0.038) and after CRF (p=0.015); the effect was confined to patients without early-life stress.
reason: Same challenge paradigm: greater dexamethasone suppression, in the same direction as enhanced negative feedback; not among the cited studies.

result: In 100 CFS vs 82 controls, routine blood values were within normal ranges, but CFS had lower RDW and higher MPV, neutrophils and neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio; overnight urine output and amino-acid excretion were lower (asparagine P<0.0001, BCAAs, phenylalanine, succinate lower; 3-methylhistidine and tyrosine higher).
reason: The paper measures blood counts and urine amino/organic acids, not the plasma metabolome. Small blood-trait differences fit omics-ukb-blood-traits, and higher MPV fits the MR MPV risk signal; the urine findings are not covered.
